tagline: Four miles through old gold country, past Jumping Off Rock.
intro: Flint Hill Road leaves Ophir Road at Ophir and runs east a little over four miles through the Uwharrie National Forest to Love Joy Road, a ten-minute drive with enough turns that the state guidebook likens it to riding in the Great Smokies. The Uwharries are thought to be among the oldest mountains in North America.

Ophir was settled in the gold boom of the mid-1800s and named for the Biblical land that sent gold to Solomon's temple. At the Steel Mine just west of Ophir, an old account says, the digging became a mania, with farmers finding gold in almost every hill.

moments.title: Ophir
moments.text: Gold is said to have turned up at that mine on the Uwharrie River around 1832, and by 1934 its ten-stamp mill sat on the site going to ruin.

moments.title: Uwharrie Trail
moments.text: The trail's northern trailhead is here, and the trail itself began in the late 1960s with an Asheboro Scoutmaster, Joe Moffitt, who wanted a fifty-mile hike close to home for his Scouts.

moments.title: Jumping Off Rock
moments.text: A quarter mile east of the trailhead a rocky bluff looks down on a cascading stream, and the guidebook strongly discourages taking the name literally.
